The Purchase and Release Specification (PRS) document for Phenoxyethanol was incorrectly assigned the number PRS0205A when the material was received from a new manufacturer.
The correct PRS number associated with Phenoxyethanol is PRS0087. Therefore, the PRS document number will be updated from PRS0205A.V01 to PRS0087B.V01, in accordance with SOP066, Section 7.1.1
As Phenoxyethanol is used as an antimicrobial preservative in the products, the material must be labelled according to the colour coding system outlined in ES.SOP.066, Appendix B. Based on this classification, a blue colour label must be attached to the material.
This labelling requirement will be incorporated into the updated PRS document.

This change will correct an incorrect Purchase and Release Specification (PRS) reference number that was assigned in error during receipt of Phenoxyethanol from a new manufacturer. 

The correct PRS number for this material is PRS0087, and the update from PRS0205A.V01 to PRS0087B.V01 aligns the documentation with the material.
 
No modifications are being made to the material specification or the manufacturing process, hence does not introduce any risk in manufacturing product with this material.

In addition, the inclusion of the blue colour identification label requirement reflects the existing material classification for Phenoxyethanol as a preservative, as defined in ES.SOP.066 Appendix B.

The update will only correct the PRS reference and existing labelling requirements in relation to potential allergens. Therefore, correcting the PRS without a change control is justified.

Addition of Opella Healthcare as an alternative company name on the Batch Manufacturing Record (BMR) for Buscopan tablets.
During review of the Patient Information Leaflet (PIL) for Buscopan tablets supplied under Sanofi and Opella Healthcare, it was confirmed that both PILs are identical in content, formulation, and product information. The only difference identified is the company name displayed on the leaflet.
As the product remains the same and is marketed under both company names following corporate restructuring, the BMR will be updated to include Opella Healthcare alongside Sanofi to accurately reflect the current product documentation.
Supporting documentation (PILs for both Sanofi and Opella Healthcare) will be attached as Appendix to this DCR.

The proposed update is administrative in nature and does not impact the product, manufacturing process, specifications, or GMP-critical documentation.
Review of the Sanofi and Opella Healthcare PILs confirmed that:
•	The product name, formulation, dosage form, strength, and instructions for use remain unchanged.
•	The content of both PIL documents is identical, with the only difference being the company name due to corporate branding changes.
•	There is no change to the product itself, manufacturing process, materials, specifications, or quality requirements.
Therefore, no brand or product assessment is required, as the tablets remain the same approved product.

The purpose of this update is to improve clarity within the PRS section Release Specification regarding testing requirements for incoming material.
The text has been revised to explicitly state that Loss on Drying and Microbial Contamination testing must be performed in-house on every batch received prior to material release, and that results must comply with the manufacturer’s specifications.
Although this requirement was introduced in Version 02 in accordance with Risk Assessment Risk.2024.017, the previous wording did not clearly specify that testing must be conducted internally before release. This update ensures unambiguous instruction and consistent application during material release activities.
Additionally, the product title has been updated from:
“Capsule Shell White (Gelatine) Size 3”
to:
“Capsule Shell White Opaque (Gelatine) Size 3”
This change aligns the internal documentation with the product name as stated on the manufacturer’s Certificate of Analysis (CoA), ensuring consistency and traceability.

Justification for why the change does not require a change control – Justify why the proposed changes should be implemented without raising a change control 
(Attach any supporting information/documentation): 

This update is considered administrative and clarificatory in nature and does not require formal change control for the following reasons:
• The requirement to perform Loss on Drying and Microbial Contamination testing on every batch was already approved and implemented under Version 02 following Risk Assessment Risk.2024.017.
• The revision does not introduce new testing requirements, acceptance criteria, or processes, but only clarifies existing expectations.
• There is no impact on product quality, safety, or efficacy, as the operational practice remains unchanged.
• The product name update is editorial, aligning documentation with the manufacturer’s CoA, with no impact on material specification, sourcing, or use.
• No changes to manufacturing process, analytical methods, specifications, or supplier are introduced.
Therefore, this update is classified as a minor documentation clarification and can be managed under document control without initiation of a formal change control process.

The internal Audit schedule will need to be updated with the following: 
To push the R&D audit to the end of the year
to replace the BC Audit with the Altenative area

The reason for this update is firstly; R&D is undergoing improvement and enhancement to its procedures with regards to formulation development. Thus, auditing this now midway through the updates being conducted would not be of any benefit and would only highlight any deficiencies we are already aware of. for this reason, it is best to shift this to the end of the year where all the enhancements will likely be completed thus an effective review of these enhancements can be conducted as part of the audit. 
The second reason regarding replacement of the BC Audit is because we have not and currently do not intent to integrate all of our wholesale activity within BC. Thus there would be nothing to audit here. So it is a sensible suggestion to replace this with an audit of an area that has not been audited directly for a while.

It is requested that the review period for ES.SOP.006.F08 – Training Record is extended from the current 2-year review cycle to a 5-year review cycle.

The current version of the form has an issue date of 14OCT24, effective date of 21OCT24 and review date of 21OCT26. The form is used to record staff training against SOP/COM documents, including the version number, date issued, date read, trainee signature, approved by and date approved fields. The form also includes a revision history section, with the previous change recorded as the addition of the form revision history following biennial review. 

No major changes are required to the content, layout or intended use of the form. The only proposed change is to extend the review date to 5 years to better align with the practical use of the form.

This change is considered minor and administrative only. The form does not define a manufacturing process, testing process, cleaning process, equipment operation or GMP control. It is a controlled template used to document training evidence.

The current 2-year review cycle can cause the form to expire before associated SOP/COM training records are fully completed or before SOP updates have been closed out. This makes the version update section less efficient, as the form may require a version change even when the form content and intended use remain unchanged.

It has also been identified that, in some cases, forms have continued to be used after the stated review date to fill training record gaps, based on previous QA advice. This was done to maintain continuity of training records where the form content had not changed. However, this DCR is being raised to formally address the issue and reduce the likelihood of recurrence.

Extending the review period to 5 years will reduce unnecessary administrative version changes, avoid making the training/version update section bulky, and ensure the form remains practical for its intended use.

There is no impact to product quality, patient safety, training requirements, GMP compliance or data integrity. The form will remain under document control, and any required change identified before the 5-year review date can still be raised through the normal document change process.
Training records already completed remain valid, as the information captured by the form has not changed. No retrospective retraining is required.
